about.body: The N52 is BMW's naturally aspirated inline-six petrol engine, in production from 2004 to 2015. It was BMW's first production engine to use magnesium-aluminium composite construction, contributing to lighter weight compared to its iron-block predecessors — a detail worth knowing if you're researching this engine's design more broadly, though our work here covers Z4 applications specifically. Within the Z4 E89 range, the N52 powered two variants — the sDrive23i (2.5L) and sDrive30i (3.0L) — across the model's second generation from 2009 to 2016.

byModel.body: Across the Z4 E89 generation (2009–2016), the N52 was fitted to the sDrive23i (2.5L) and sDrive30i (3.0L) variants. The sDrive30i used the 3.0L version of the N52, while the sDrive23i used the 2.5L version — two distinct capacities sharing the same engine family, both covered by our rebuild service.

compatibility.body: Because the N52 was fitted in different capacities across the Z4 E89 range — 2.5L in the sDrive23i and 3.0L in the sDrive30i — compatibility comes down to confirming your exact variant, which we do by registration. A 3.0L N52 from an sDrive30i isn't a direct replacement for a 2.5L N52 from an sDrive23i, even though they share the same base engine family — ancillaries and internal components differ. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm your exact vehicle.
